item.title: Said & Checked, Oregon, 2026-11-20: none false or contradicted, 4 unsettled (Jeff Merkley)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Jeff Merkley, U.S. Senator: “One of the provisions of this bill essentially says that if you use dirty jet engines to power your data center, they will be exempted from the clean air and noise provisions.” Unsettled. The introduced text of S. 5653 contains no exemption of data-center turbines from Clean Air Act or noise requirements and only one Clean Air Act reference, a savings clause; the Senate-passed text with the managers' amendment, which the debate concerned, could not be read directly.
  • Jeff Merkley, U.S. Senator: “the President was saying: Wind power is a national emergency, in order to prepare to put tariffs on wind components so those wind farms can't be built regardless of what is done in this bill.” Unsettled. Trump's October 2026 Section 232 proclamation found that imported wind turbines and parts threaten to impair national security and opened 180 days of negotiations with tariffs possible later, but it does not use the term national emergency.
  • Jeff Merkley, U.S. Senator: “My State is on fire. The Cascade snowpack has dropped by 40 percent.” Unsettled. AskAmerica's SNOTEL data show Oregon's April 1, 2026 snowpack far below median, from about 5% in the Willamette basin to 40% in the Hood basin, while the warehouse does not reach back far enough to test a long-term 40% decline; the figure depends on which period is meant.
